direction-type.words: This major chord is derived from the chromatic lowering
of the second degree of the scale in a minor or harmonic major.
Used in the form of sixth chord with doubled the third, and
resolves to the tonic six-four chord or a tonic triad.
Also, this chord is sometimes used after the tonic triad.
Dominant seventh chord with a lowered fifth
Chromatic lowering of the second degree of the scale allows you
to form a dominant seventh chord with a lowered fifth.
R-K's remark: these chords should be used sparingly.
